component_findings.dependency_metadata: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--c): vcpkg release cadence and volume: <cite index="42-3,42-4,42-5">302 ports were updated in July... as part of the 2026.07.29 registry release and the 2026-07-13, 2026-07-24, and 2026-07-27 tool releases, these updates include major SBOM improvements in vcpkg-tool, 302 updated ports including multiple major library upgrades</cite>. Earlier months show similarly high churn: <cite index="47-3,47-6">521 ports were updated in May... This release includes major library updates for Boost 1.91, Qt 6.11, and OpenCASCADE 8.0, along with 27 new ports and over 500 port updates</cite>, and <cite index="49-3">415 ports were updated in February and 321 ports were updated in March</cite>.
component_findings.distribution_artifacts: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--c): 85/100. The dominant curated registry (vcpkg) demonstrates near-continuous, high-volume maintenance (hundreds of port updates monthly, monthly release cadence, steady net growth), and flagship domain libraries (Boost, Asio, nlohmann/json, gRPC, Dlib) all show recent, dated, substantive releases within the last 6-18 months. Score is not higher because C++ package activity is split across multiple non-interoperable package managers (vcpkg, Conan, Spack, system managers) rather than one unified registry, which dilutes any single ecosystem-wide activity signal and increases the risk of stale or duplicate/abandoned recipes across registries relative to ecosystems with one authoritative, first-par

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.limitations: Port-update counts and GitHub stars/forks are disclosed as raw, consistently-collected proxies alongside dated release evidence; they are not used as the sole basis for the score.
metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.selection_rule: Use the primary package registry/ecosystem for the language when one exists and evaluate current observable maintenance within the fixed activity window; package count alone is never sufficient.

component_findings.data_numerical: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--c): Foundational/general-purpose domain: Boost is treated as a standards-adjacent reference; <cite index="25-2">Beginning with the ten Boost Libraries included in the Library Technical Report (TR1) and continuing with every release of the ISO standard for C++ since 2011, the C++ Standards Committee has continued to rely on Boost as a valuable source for additions to the Standard C++ Library.</cite> Boost itself spans linear algebra, threading, image processing, regex, and unit testing in one umbrella: <cite index="24-1">The Boost C++ Libraries (also known simply as Boost) are a set of libraries for the C++ programming language that provides support for tasks and structures such as linear algebra
component_findings.ml_ai: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--c): vcpkg registry breadth: <cite index="42-1,42-2">There are now 2,858 total ports available in the vcpkg curated registry, a port is a versioned recipe for building a package from source, such as a C or C++ library.</cite> Microsoft's own overview states <cite index="20-5">Over 2300 open-source libraries to choose from in a curated registry, routinely built to verify ABI compatibility.</cite>

metric.third_party_library_availability_.limitations: Port/recipe counts and presence in vcpkg/ConanCenter are used only as declared, disclosed evidence of breadth, not as the sole scoring input; qualitative domain-by-domain library maturity and standards-adjacency were the primary basis for the score.
metric.third_party_library_availability_.selection_rule: Inspect the same five fixed domain groups for every language; prefer the official package index or official ecosystem directory, then independent package/project evidence.
